classification.difficultyReason: Identify several boundary equations and combine their shaded half-planes, distinguishing solid and dashed boundaries.

content.prompt: Write down the inequalities whose intersections are the shaded region.

spec.description: Two solid boundaries with marked intercepts; the region below both is shaded. Source vertical hatching is represented by a light blue region fill. Origin letter omitted under house graph rules.
spec.mathematics: Boundaries y=x+2 and y=2-x; marked points (-2,0), (0,2), (2,0).
spec.answerVisibility: All supplied geometry remains visible; inequalities appear only in answers.

answer.worked:
The boundary through $(-2,0)$ and $(0,2)$ is $y=x+2$. The other boundary is $y=2-x$. The shading is below both solid lines, so both boundaries are included:
$$x+y\le2,\qquad y-x\le2.$$

spec.description: Two solid rising boundaries and their marked intercepts; the intersection region between them to the right is light blue.
spec.mathematics: Boundaries y=3x+3 and y=x-1 intersect at (-2,-3).
spec.answerVisibility: Boundary equations and intersection coordinates are not printed on the question diagram.

answer.worked:
For the steeper boundary:
$$\begin{align*}m&=\frac{3-0}{0-(-1)}\\m&=3.\end{align*}$$
Its equation is $y=3x+3$. The shallower boundary has intercepts $(0,-1)$ and $(1,0)$, so its equation is $y=x-1$. The shading lies above the shallower line and below the steeper line. Both are solid:
$$y\ge x-1,\qquad y\le3x+3.$$

spec.description: Solid horizontal boundary, dashed red vertical boundary, open intersection and region above and left.
spec.mathematics: Horizontal boundary y=2; vertical boundary x=2; intersection excluded.
spec.answerVisibility: Given boundaries and shading remain visible.

answer.worked: The region is above the solid line $y=2$, so $y\ge2$. It is left of the dashed line $x=2$, so $x<2$. The open corner is excluded.

spec.description: Solid rising diagonal through the marked origin and open labelled corner; dashed horizontal boundary; region above the diagonal and below the horizontal.
spec.mathematics: Boundaries y=x and y=2; corner (2,2) excluded.

answer.worked: The solid diagonal through $(0,0)$ and $(2,2)$ is $y=x$. The shading is above it, giving $y\ge x$. The shading is below the dashed horizontal boundary, giving $y<2$.

spec.description: Shaded triangle bounded by the x-axis, solid rising diagonal and solid vertical line. Marked origin, vertical intercept and labelled corner.
spec.mathematics: Vertices (0,0), (2,0), (2,2); boundaries y=0, y=x and x=2.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the source-supplied corner coordinate is labelled.

answer.worked:
The shading is below the diagonal $y=x$, left of $x=2$ and above the $x$-axis. All boundaries are solid, so
$$y\le x,\qquad x\le2,\qquad y\ge0.$$

spec.description: Shaded first-quadrant region bounded by both axes, the solid vertical line and solid descending diagonal, retaining all five source point markers.
spec.mathematics: Descending boundary x+y=6; vertical boundary x=3; region vertices (0,0), (3,0), (3,3), (0,6).
spec.answerVisibility: Only source-supplied intercept labels and (3,3) are printed.

answer.worked:
The diagonal has intercepts $(0,6)$ and $(6,0)$, so its equation is $x+y=6$. The shading is in the first quadrant, left of $x=3$ and below the diagonal. All boundaries are included:
$$x\ge0,\qquad y\ge0,\qquad x\le3,\qquad x+y\le6.$$
